subject: Genetics
title: Newborn Screening
description: A short lesson to help you apply Newborn Screening.

hook.text: Within 48 hours of birth, a heel prick screens for up to 50 conditions. Most parents barely notice.

buildup.text: Robert Guthrie pioneered the test in 1963 for PKU. A cheap filter card saved thousands from brain damage.

discovery.text: Today, panels screen for metabolic, endocrine, and blood disorders. Most are treatable if caught early.

twist.text: Some states store blood spots for decades. Police and researchers have used them without consent.

climax.text: Newborn screening is one of public health's greatest wins. Early detection turns fatal diseases into manageable ones.

punchline.text: A heel prick at birth. Lives saved by the thousands.
